title: The Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1968-08-22
lineage: Master Reel > ? > DAT > Panasonic SV-3700 > Korg MR-1 DSD [1 Bit/2.8 Mhz] Mastering: AudioGate to [24/96] > WaveLab > Nomad Blue Tube Limiter LM2S-3 >  AudioGate to [16/44.1] > CD Wave > TLH > Flac

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with clear audio delivers a fiery St. Stephen‑Eleven‑Dark Star stretch, though the tape is missing material from the full 8/22 show.
ai_review.review: The koucky soundboard capture presents a tight, high‑energy performance highlighted by an inspiring duel in The Eleven, a masterful Dark Star, and a dynamite Other One that rolls straight into New Potato. While the audio quality is good and the mix balances Jerry’s vocals and the organ nicely, the recording only contains the second half of the concert and omits several key numbers, so listeners may prefer the more complete Cotsman version.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers praise the musical peaks and soundboard clarity but note the incomplete set, leading to a strong yet slightly reduced overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear soundboard mix with good instrument separation; however the tape is missing material from the full show and appears to contain part of an adjacent date, causing confusion about completeness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong early set with smooth transitions (St. Stephen → The Eleven → Death), leading into a high‑impact second half featuring Dark Star and an explosive Other One that flows into New Potato.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals start low on St. Stephen but rise powerfully on Death; guitar tone described as perfect and "zooming" during The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: Engages in a duel with Jerry on The Eleven, "zooming" throughout, and delivers an extended bass solo rare after 1974.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ provides perfect embellishments, especially on Death Don't Have No Mercy.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann is described as "going nuts" on the drums during The Other One.
